open_points.subject: Owner authentication path
open_points.text: Reaches the kernel through the agent channel with the owner's token.
open_points.question: How does the kernel receive an owner's decision through an agent-controlled channel without exposing the owner token or allowing the agent to originate that decision?
options: The owner connects directly over MCP
A trusted client signs and forwards owner decisions
The agent transports an independently authenticated owner response
open_points.default_guess: Require an independently authenticated owner response that the agent cannot create or read.

open_points.subject: Installation administration
open_points.text: tokens live in the installation's protected configuration; an installation selects one manifest instance per service
open_points.question: Which actor may install, rotate or remove tokens and credentials, select service instances, and update the manifest?
options: The owner
A separate installation operator
An external deployment system
open_points.default_guess: Treat the installation operator as a separate trusted actor acting outside the kernel.

open_points.subject: Manifest authority
open_points.text: Microservices — known only as records of the platform manifest.
open_points.question: Where does the manifest come from, who is trusted to change it, and how does the kernel authenticate and validate the manifest it reads?
options: A protected local file managed by the operator
A signed manifest supplied by the platform
A trusted platform API
open_points.default_guess: Use an operator-managed protected local manifest and treat changes as trusted configuration changes.

open_points.subject: Reverse-proxy trust
open_points.text: one inbound channel, `mcp`, behind the host's reverse proxy
open_points.question: Which security properties does the kernel rely on the reverse proxy to provide besides brute-force protection, such as TLS termination, client identity headers, request-size limits or source filtering?
options: Only transport and brute-force protection
TLS and request limits, with tokens still checked by the kernel
Proxy-authenticated identities trusted by the kernel
open_points.default_guess: Trust the proxy for TLS and request limits only; validate all owner and agent tokens in the kernel.

open_points.subject: Microservice connection security
open_points.text: the kernel calls microservices over their HTTP APIs
open_points.question: How are service endpoints authenticated and protected in transit, and is an HTTP redirect or endpoint change allowed to receive credentials or data?
options: Mutually authenticated TLS with redirects refused
HTTPS with bearer credentials and redirects refused
Trusted private-network HTTP
open_points.default_guess: Require HTTPS, validate the server identity, and refuse redirects.

open_points.subject: Secret echo handling
open_points.text: A service's own answer that echoes one verbatim is withheld
open_points.question: What observable node and run result is produced when a service answer is withheld for echoing a secret, and may any digest, metadata or reason be returned?
options: Fail the node and run with a non-secret reason
Treat it as an invalid service response
Rest the run for owner intervention
open_points.default_guess: Fail the node as an invalid service response and expose only a non-secret reason.

open_points.subject: Submission of outside material
open_points.text: until the owner or an agent submits it
open_points.question: Which product action submits outside material that is already in a service intake, what identifier or value it accepts, and what success and refusal outputs it has?
options: It is an input to run a flow
It is a declared operation node in a flow
There is a separate intake-submission action
open_points.default_guess: Represent submission as a flow input containing the intake record identifier, consumed by a declared operation node.

open_points.subject: MCP operation set
open_points.text: The kernel exposes one fixed set of typed operations over `mcp`: inspect, author, try, run, resume, read traces, and the owner's approve, accept, activate, grant, revoke, resolve and cancel.
open_points.question: How are the listed primary actions add a trial case, capture a failed execution, release a failed run, roll back a slot, propose a binding, and compose and prove a flow exposed, given that they are absent from the declared fixed MCP set?
options: They are distinct missing MCP operations
They are named variants of `author`
The K-11 list is only categories and must map every action explicitly
open_points.default_guess: Treat the K-11 names as categories and specify an explicit typed operation or variant for every primary action.

open_points.subject: Agent activation
open_points.text: the owner's approve, accept, activate, grant, revoke, resolve and cancel
open_points.question: May an agent invoke the activate action for a proven read-only flow, as the primary action and K-08 say, or is activate an owner-only MCP operation?
options: Agents may request activation only for proven read-only versions
Only the owner may invoke activate
Agents use a separate request-activation operation
open_points.default_guess: Allow an agent to invoke activate only for a proven read-only version.

open_points.subject: Trying implementations
open_points.text: try an implementation | agent
open_points.question: May an agent without the author right supply or execute new code in a trial, or may it only try an already stored implementation?
options: Only author-capable agents may submit new code; all agents may retry stored implementations
Only author-capable agents may try implementations
Every agent may submit code for trial but cannot store it
open_points.default_guess: Only author-capable agents may supply code; any agent may request a trial of stored code.

open_points.subject: Failed-execution capture
open_points.text: the trial case every later implementation must pass
open_points.question: How can a failed real execution become a passing trial case when the action supplies no expected output or expected verdict for the repaired implementation?
options: The caller supplies the expected output
The case asserts only that the execution must not fail
The owner later completes the captured case
open_points.default_guess: Require the capturing caller to supply the expected output and validate it against the contract.

open_points.subject: Corpus change and active implementation
open_points.text: add a trial case
open_points.question: When a case is added or captured, is the active implementation automatically re-admitted over the enlarged corpus, deactivated if it fails, or allowed to remain active without a current admission verdict?
options: Re-admit immediately and deactivate on failure
Keep the activation but prevent new runs until re-admitted
Apply new cases only to later implementation submissions
open_points.default_guess: Re-admit the active implementation immediately and deactivate it if the enlarged corpus fails.

open_points.subject: Contract-version transition
open_points.text: author a function contract or implementation
open_points.question: What makes a newly authored contract version the slot's current contract version, and what happens to the prior implementation activation and flows referring to the prior version?
options: Authoring automatically makes it current
A separate contract-activation action selects it
Slots have no current contract version and all references are explicit
open_points.default_guess: Use explicit contract-version references and remove the undefined notion of a slot-wide current contract version.

open_points.subject: Flow proof diagnostic order
open_points.text: the first failing edge or node
open_points.question: What deterministic ordering defines the first failure when several edges or nodes fail proof?
options: Canonical node and edge identifier order
Stored graph declaration order
Topological order with a specified tie-breaker
open_points.default_guess: Use topological order with a canonical identifier tie-breaker.

open_points.subject: Flow input and output
open_points.text: run a flow | owner, agent | a run of the flow's active version, with outputs
open_points.question: What inputs does run accept, how are they matched to the flow interface, and which terminal node values constitute the returned flow outputs?
options: Flows declare typed named input and output ports
Runs accept no caller input and expose all sink-node outputs
Special source and sink nodes define the interface
open_points.default_guess: Require every flow version to declare typed named value inputs and outputs mapped to graph ports.

open_points.subject: Run terminal result
open_points.text: a failed node stops its dependants
open_points.question: How is the run's terminal status and output determined when one branch fails while independent branches succeed, or when some nodes are skipped as dependants?
options: Any failed node makes the run failed after runnable branches finish
The first failure ends the whole run
Partial success is a separate terminal status
open_points.default_guess: Continue independent branches, then end the run failed and retain their outputs in the trace but not as successful flow outputs.

open_points.subject: Approval send outcomes
open_points.text: the effect runs on the exact input shown
open_points.question: What does approve return when the exact request cannot be sent, the service rejects it, validation fails, or the response leaves the outcome unknown?
options: Return the updated run and its waiting or terminal status
Return a typed effect-attempt result
Refuse the approval action itself
open_points.default_guess: Accept the decision, create an effect attempt, and return the updated run with pending, failed or continued status.

open_points.subject: Approval eligibility
open_points.text: an approval of a run that has ended can no longer be decided
open_points.question: What happens when the run is live but the named attempt is absent, already decided, not awaiting approval, or the supplied decision does not identify the exact shown request?
options: Refuse with a reason
Return the prior decision idempotently
Resolve by run and next pending effect
open_points.default_guess: Require an exact pending approval identifier and refuse absent, stale or already decided requests with a reason.

open_points.subject: Cancellation during invocation
open_points.text: the run ends `cancelled`; nothing further is sent
open_points.question: What happens if cancellation races with an operation request already being constructed or sent, and how is an in-flight request whose outcome is unknown recorded?
options: Cancellation is allowed only when no request is in flight
Already-started sends complete and may leave an unknown attempt
The transport is forcibly aborted and treated as unknown
open_points.default_guess: Stop new sends, allow an already-started send to settle, and record it as unknown if its outcome cannot be established.

open_points.subject: Trace lookup
open_points.text: read a trace | owner, agent | trace records | —
open_points.question: What is returned for an unknown run or trace reference, a released failed run whose files are gone, or a trace value the caller is not allowed to see?
options: Unknown references are refused and unavailable values are represented explicitly
Return an empty result
Trace reads never use direct references
open_points.default_guess: Refuse unknown references and return metadata with an explicit unavailable-file marker where only spool content was released.

open_points.subject: Effect metadata
open_points.text: Effect classes are `read`, `draft-write`, `state-transition`, `external-effect`, `destructive`.
open_points.question: Where is an operation's effect class declared, who may set it, and what authoritative evidence prevents an agent from binding an effectful service operation as `read`?
options: The trusted platform manifest declares it
The binding proposer declares it and the owner verifies it
The kernel derives it from the HTTP operation
open_points.default_guess: Require the trusted manifest operation record to declare the effect class and make the binding copy that pinned declaration.

open_points.subject: Idempotency declaration
open_points.text: The kernel supplies the declared idempotency key
open_points.question: Where and how does an operation declare the idempotency-key location and semantics, and which effect classes are required to support it?
options: The manifest operation declares a header or body field
Every effect uses a fixed kernel header
The accepted binding declares the mapping
open_points.default_guess: Put the key mapping and support declaration in the pinned manifest operation record.

open_points.subject: Unknown applied outcome
open_points.text: the run continues
open_points.question: When the owner resolves an unknown effect as applied, where does the operation's output come from if downstream nodes require it?
options: Effect operations with unknown outcomes may not have downstream outputs
The owner supplies a validated output during resolution
The kernel performs a read-only result lookup declared by the operation
open_points.default_guess: Require the owner to supply a schema-valid output during resolution when downstream execution needs one.

open_points.subject: Unreachable versus unknown
open_points.text: pending when a service is unreachable or an outcome unknown
open_points.question: What observable transport events classify an invocation as safely unreachable and resumable versus possibly sent with an unknown outcome requiring owner resolution?
options: Failure before any bytes are sent is unreachable; any later ambiguity is unknown
Only connection-establishment failure is unreachable
Each manifest operation declares the classification rules
open_points.default_guess: Treat a verified failure before sending request bytes as unreachable and every ambiguity after sending begins as outcome unknown.

open_points.subject: Standing-grant eligibility
open_points.text: grant a standing approval for a node ... a `destructive` node ... cannot be granted
open_points.question: Can grants be created for `read` or `draft-write` nodes that never ask at run time, or only for `state-transition` and `external-effect` nodes?
options: Only state-transition and external-effect nodes
Every non-destructive operation node
Any node, including function nodes
open_points.default_guess: Allow grants only for state-transition and external-effect operation nodes.

open_points.subject: Standing-grant lifecycle
open_points.text: for a node of a flow's active version
open_points.question: When another flow version is activated, is the old version's grant revoked, merely inactive, or retained so that it revives if that version is activated again?
options: Revoke grants when the version ceases to be active
Retain but suspend them and revive on rollback
Retain them but require fresh confirmation on reactivation
open_points.default_guess: Revoke grants when their flow version ceases to be active.

open_points.subject: Function file production
open_points.text: no filesystem beyond its input
open_points.question: How can a function produce a file output, which K-06 explicitly permits, if it cannot write beyond its input filesystem?
options: A separate writable output mount is allowed
A file is returned as bounded bytes through standard output
Function file outputs are removed from the model
open_points.default_guess: Provide a bounded writable output area whose declared files are collected as output ports.

open_points.subject: Caller value classification
open_points.text: Every value carries `open`, `business_confidential` or `personal_data`.
open_points.question: Who assigns and validates the disclosure class of caller-supplied flow inputs and trial-case values so that an agent cannot label personal data as open?
options: Only the owner may classify caller values
The flow input declaration fixes the class
Values must originate from bindings or trusted stored fixtures
open_points.default_guess: Have each flow input or contract fixture declaration set a minimum class, with only the owner allowed to raise or supply personal-data values.

open_points.subject: Proof validity
open_points.text: The kernel proves it whole before it can run
open_points.question: Which changes invalidate or require recomputation of a stored proof, including a new contract version, activation change, binding replacement, manifest digest change or disclosure declaration change?
options: Proofs pin every referenced immutable version and remain valid
Proofs are recomputed at every activation and run
Specific dependency changes invalidate a proof
open_points.default_guess: Pin every immutable contract, binding and flow-interface declaration in the proof, while treating a manifest digest mismatch as an invocation refusal rather than proof mutation.

open_points.subject: Photo-upload acceptance path
open_points.text: A flow takes an original invoice photo into custody through the owning service's declared operations; it shows effect classes, the owner's approval on the exact input, the idempotency key and `pending`.
open_points.question: Which real services and operations form the flow, where the photo starts and ends, which operation requires approval, and whether `pending` must mean unreachable service or unknown outcome?
options: Specify a concrete fixture manifest and expected run sequence
Name deployment-provided roles with a conformance contract
Use any available services satisfying stated capabilities
open_points.default_guess: Specify a concrete fixture manifest, operation sequence, exact approval request, and an induced unknown-outcome pending state.

open_points.subject: Photo-upload completion criterion
open_points.text: it shows effect classes, the owner's approval on the exact input, the idempotency key and `pending`
open_points.question: What final observable result makes the acceptance case pass after the run reaches pending, including whether the owner resolves it and where custody is verified?
options: Reaching pending with the expected trace is sufficient
Resolve applied and verify the destination service owns the photo
Resolve not applied, reapprove and verify a single successful send
open_points.default_guess: Resolve not applied, require a fresh approval, complete the run, and verify custody in the owning service with one applied idempotency key.

open_points.subject: Analysis acceptance oracle
open_points.text: Within one conversation the agent writes the missing functions, tries and admits them, composes a read-only flow over declared read operations and returns an analysis, releasing nothing.
open_points.question: What concrete input, service operations, missing functions, expected analysis and machine-observable pass condition define this case?
options: Provide fixed fixtures and an exact expected value
Provide fixtures and a deterministic predicate over the result
Use a human judgment of analysis quality
open_points.default_guess: Provide fixed service fixtures, contracts, trial cases and an exact deterministic expected analysis value.

open_points.subject: Conversation boundary
open_points.text: Within one conversation
open_points.question: What begins and ends the conversation, and what persisted state or prior setup is allowed when measuring this acceptance condition?
options: One MCP session from an empty kernel fixture
One agent transcript across reconnects
A human-observed interaction with preloaded contracts and bindings
open_points.default_guess: Define it as one MCP session against a specified initial kernel and manifest fixture.

open_points.subject: Negative acceptance matrix
open_points.text: each refusal of K-05 through K-09 is shown by a bounded negative case
open_points.question: What exact enumerable list of refusals and expected codes or state transitions must the negative cases cover?
options: List every normative refusal in K-05 through K-09
Cover one representative refusal per decision
Derive cases from a later formal rule catalogue
open_points.default_guess: Create an explicit matrix containing every refusal condition stated in K-05 through K-09 and its expected observable result.

open_points.subject: Real service instances
open_points.text: both cases pass against the real service instances
open_points.question: Which service instances, versions, initial data and reset procedure constitute the acceptance environment?
options: Named disposable rig instances with fixed versions and fixtures
Any installation satisfying a conformance profile
Production instances with isolated test records
open_points.default_guess: Use named disposable rig instances pinned to versions and reset from fixed fixtures.

open_points.subject: Sandbox standard library
open_points.text: the Python standard library only
open_points.question: Which standard-library modules and capabilities are actually usable, given that the standard library includes network, process, filesystem, clock and randomness APIs forbidden by K-02?
options: Allow imports but enforce capability denial at runtime
Specify an allowlist of safe modules
Permit the whole standard library and rely only on sandbox isolation
open_points.default_guess: Specify a safe-module allowlist and also enforce the capability restrictions in the sandbox.

open_points.subject: External photo processing
open_points.text: the agent processes a photo itself, outside the kernel
open_points.question: How can the agent obtain and process that photo consistently with the rule that personal-data values never reach an agent, and which system is responsible for authorizing and auditing this out-of-kernel access?
options: Photos in this case are not personal_data
Only the owner processes personal-data photos
An external agent tool receives service data under a separate trust model
open_points.default_guess: Do not permit agent processing when the photo is personal_data; require owner processing or a declared service operation.
